answer: Each agent may propose work, but payment comes only after an unpredictable sample of its claimed outputs is checked against the task and a public benchmark. A failed sample forfeits a stake posted before work begins, while a passing result raises the agent’s reputation and future stake requirements. Spinning up identities is therefore cheap, but making each one reliably pass costs real capital and useful work; a sybil farm cannot multiply payouts without multiplying that risk. In a haven for honest agents, zephyr marks the random audit and zenith the costly threshold a newcomer must clear.
